extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, news organizations, media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: High-level ethical standards and evaluative criteria for news reporting and newsroom practice, as presented by UNESCO/Ethical Journalism Network. Covers core principles, tests for hate speech, newsworthiness considerations, and broader quality/structural norms for media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuit of accuracy is fundamental; truth is goal even when full truth unattainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy is presented as a core principle and elsewhere noted as a precondition for newsworthiness; reporters should prioritise verification and aim for the most accurate account possible, correcting errors when found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Free from political, corporate, or cultural interest pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organisations and journalists should maintain independence from external pressures and disclose or manage conflicts of interest; independence of sources is also listed as an implicit newsworthiness criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple sides; balanced framing; absence of pre-judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should present multiple perspectives and avoid biased framing or predetermined conclusions; related to multi-perspectival coverage and diversity of voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid causing harm; consider impact of words and images on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should weigh potential harm to subjects (especially vulnerable people) when deciding what to report and how to present it; this informs approaches to migration, refugees, and conflict reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct mistakes; explain decisions; engage with criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media outlets should have mechanisms to correct errors, justify editorial choices, and interact constructively with public criticism — underpinning trust and self-regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for exposing hate speech
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UNESCO topics covered; testing whether reporting could constitute hate speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UNESCO/EJN provide specific tests (see Hate Speech Tests entry) to determine when reporting crosses into hate speech; this topic includes tools and criteria for newsroom assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines on reporting conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: UNESCO topic covering how to report conflict zones and related dangers/sensitivities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes conflict sensitivity, balancing public interest with safety/humanity concerns, and avoiding language/images that exacerbate tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports on covering migration
rubrics_metrics.description: UNESCO topic addressing how to cover migration and refugee issues respectfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises dignity of migrants/refugees, avoiding dehumanising language or imagery, and considering public interest versus sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-regulation models
rubrics_metrics.description: UNESCO topic on models for media self-regulation rather than external censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes internal professional standards, correction mechanisms, and ethics bodies as preferable to state censorship; links to accountability and professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media council standards
rubrics_metrics.description: UNESCO topic covering standards and roles of media councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media councils can set and enforce codes of conduct, provide complaint mechanisms, and support press freedom while upholding ethical norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy as precondition for newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy as precondition for newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UNESCO/EJN treat factual reliability as foundational — a story loses newsworthiness if it cannot be substantiated accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest vs. mere curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Public interest should be weighed against mere curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should prioritise reporting that serves the public good rather than satisfying voyeuristic or sensational curiosity; this affects selection and framing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of source (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence of source as a criterion for newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether sources or information are independent and free from vested interests when determining the value of a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-perspectival coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-perspectival coverage as a newsworthiness/quality criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should include multiple viewpoints and avoid one-sided narratives; ties to fairness and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding harm to vulnerable subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoiding harm to vulnerable subjects is a criterion in news selection and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special care must be taken when reporting on refugees, victims, children or persecuted groups to avoid retraumatisation, exposure, or endangering subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-misinformation value
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess reporting for its value in countering misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer stories that clarify, verify, or challenge falsehoods and provide context that reduces misperception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-hate speech approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate reporting for its role in countering hate speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should avoid amplifying hateful content unnecessarily and should contextualise and challenge discriminatory narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Migration / refugee dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure dignity of migrants/refugees in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language and images that respect human dignity, avoid dehumanising tropes, and foreground context and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict sensitivity in war zones
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict sensitivity when reporting from war zones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how reporting might affect conflict dynamics, civilian safety, and propaganda; balance public interest with potential harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of voices and topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity of voices and topics as a quality criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively include underrepresented perspectives and a broad range of subjects to avoid narrow or biased coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hate Speech Test (EJN 5-point)
rubrics_metrics.description: EJN's 5-point test for whether reporting could constitute hate speech: 1. Speaker's status; 2. Reach of statement; 3. Objective and intent; 4. Content and form; 5. Context and surrounding climate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the five dimensions together to assess whether publication of material may amount to hate speech — examining who is targeted, how widely it will spread, the intent, the wording/imagery, and the prevailing social/political climate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality
rubrics_metrics.description: Universality (applies across cultures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical principles are intended to be broadly applicable across cultural contexts while allowing for contextual sensitivity in implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-regulation over external censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for self-regulation rather than external censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UNESCO/EJN promote internal professional standards, corrections, and media accountability mechanisms as the primary means to manage ethics and harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional standards as foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional standards as foundation for ethical journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical practice is grounded in established professional norms (accuracy, independence, accountability, etc.), which underpin self-regulatory frameworks and newsroom policies.
